events.title: Nerva Becomes Emperor of Rome
events.description: After the assassination of the unpopular emperor Domitian, the Roman Senate declared the elderly senator Nerva emperor. The Senate also cancelled Domitian's decrees and ordered his statues torn down.
events.significance: Nerva's accession began the era of the 'Five Good Emperors', a period of relative stability and prosperity that lasted for most of the next century.

events.title: Muslim Forces Capture Damascus
events.description: Rashidun Arab forces under the general Khalid ibn al-Walid took Damascus from the Byzantine Empire after a siege.
events.significance: The fall of Damascus was a major step in the early Islamic conquest of the Levant and shifted the balance of power in the region.

events.title: Battle of Poitiers
events.description: At Poitiers in France, an English army led by Edward the Black Prince defeated a larger French force. The English captured King John II of France.
events.significance: The capture of the French king was a disaster for France during the Hundred Years' War. It led to a huge ransom and deep political turmoil.

events.title: Jamestown Burned in Bacon's Rebellion
events.description: Forces led by Nathaniel Bacon set fire to Jamestown, Virginia, the capital of the colony. Bacon was in revolt against the colonial governor.
events.significance: The burning of Jamestown was a dramatic peak of one of colonial America's earliest major uprisings against royal authority.

events.title: Battle of Chickamauga Begins
events.description: The first day of fighting took place near Chickamauga Creek in northwestern Georgia during the American Civil War. The battle became the bloodiest two-day engagement of the war.
events.significance: It was the Confederacy's most significant victory in the Western Theater, although the Union kept control of the key city of Chattanooga.
